Telescope 3.6 polishes the desktop app's look and makes streaming a lot smoother when the Wi-Fi isn't great.

## New

**A cleaner window.** This refines the look 3.0 brought in, card by card. The goal was a window that's easier to use and quicker to scan, and one you can use entirely from the keyboard, which makes Telescope a lot more accessible too. Checkboxes became switches, resolution and frame rate are tiles and every card has its own colour (**Card colours** in Advanced sets it back to all purple). Tab goes through everything in reading order, focus rings show up when you're using the keyboard and every control has a name for screen readers. Advanced, Keyboard shortcuts and Plugins got the same one row per setting layout with shorter tooltips.

**UDP on Wi-Fi (experimental).** A switch in the Connection card sends Light over UDP. On busy Wi-Fi a lost packet then only means resending that one piece instead of holding up the whole stream. If nothing gets through (usually a firewall) it goes back to TCP. It doesn't work with Dynamic or Heavy yet. My own Wi-Fi is too quiet to show a difference so I'd love to hear how it does on a crowded one.

**Hardware acceleration.** A switch in Advanced decodes Light on the graphics card, mostly worth it at 4K or on a laptop. AMD and Intel cards on Linux need VA-API and **Set up VA-API…** next to the switch gets it for you. I couldn't try it on Windows with a real graphics card so please report it if it doesn't work there.

**Auto level** in the Microphone card evens out quiet and loud speech without turning up the room noise in the pauses.

## Smoother streaming

- No more mic clicks when the phone's clock and the computer's drift apart, and less mic delay overall.
- Plugging in the cable mid-stream moves to USB without a gap.
- The phone uses H.264's High profile when it can, which looks a bit sharper at the same bitrate.
- Dynamic handles really slow links better and changes the frame rate without restarting the camera.
- A phone that gets too hot lowers its frame rate instead of heating up until the alert stops the stream.
- The phone keeps its screen and Wi-Fi awake while Telescope is open to avoid lag spikes (the power button still turns the screen off).
- Streams start a little sooner and recover about a second faster after a Wi-Fi drop.
- The desktop uses a lot less CPU while streaming and on Linux noticeably less RAM too, especially during longer sessions.

## Fixed

- The phone mic stayed quiet after Android's audio system restarted.
- The phone app sometimes couldn't be found after it was reopened quickly.
- Stopping on the phone and leaving the app right away showed up on the desktop as a dropped stream.
- Saved keyboard shortcuts and arrow key panning didn't work, and the shortcuts plugin could crash.
- Some windows opened behind the main window.

Keep the phone app and the desktop on the same version since most of this needs both. Found something broken? Open an issue and paste your **Copy diagnostics** report into it.
